title: Issues with writing file names
body:
Hi, great tool!

I just starting trying it, and I'm running into some issues. 

Initially, I was encountering the same problem as detailed in this issue: https://github.com/AntonOsika/gpt-engineer/issues/167. Fortunately, I noticed you fixed this and after pulling the changes, that issue was resolved.

However, I'm now facing another issue related to file name generation. The program is formatting file names as '`filename`':
![image](https://github.com/AntonOsika/gpt-engineer/assets/25695071/6fe9db63-3b14-481d-8182-8c8ed5e9f75f)

At other (most) times, it's formatting them as '[filename]', which is resulting in file outputs like this:

![image](https://github.com/AntonOsika/gpt-engineer/assets/25695071/801f1da0-6968-4001-9bba-882d0db40c42)

I suspect this might have something to do with this commit: https://github.com/AntonOsika/gpt-engineer/commit/8180f0346c8a380637b72212432aa9abd5c04a9c#diff-945067bb601867dd64fd5ae92de9bf829da8545700835ac49744902ddec355fd

I'm using gpt-3.5-turbo since I don't have access to gpt-4 yet. Maybe the model is not as smart to understand this prompt?

linked_prs.title: Fix square bracket file name issue
linked_prs.patch:
diff --git a/gpt_engineer/chat_to_files.py b/gpt_engineer/chat_to_files.py
index a043eae..f4812d4 100644
--- a/gpt_engineer/chat_to_files.py
+++ b/gpt_engineer/chat_to_files.py
@@ -11,6 +11,9 @@ def parse_chat(chat):  # -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
         # Strip the filename of any non-allowed characters and convert / to \
         path = re.sub(r'[<>"|?*]', "", match.group(1))
 
+        # Remove leading and trailing brackets
+        path = re.sub(r"^\[(.*)\]$", r"\1", path)
+
         # Get the code
         code = match.group(2)
 
diff --git a/tests/test_chat_to_files.py b/tests/test_chat_to_files.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..176c19b
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_chat_to_files.py
@@ -0,0 +1,94 @@
+import textwrap
+
+from gpt_engineer.chat_to_files import to_files
+
+
+def test_to_files():
+    chat = textwrap.dedent(
+        """
+    This is a sample program.
+
+    file1.py
+    ```python
+    print("Hello, World!")
+    ```
+
+    file2.py
+    ```python
+    def add(a, b):
+        return a + b
+    ```
+    """
+    )
+
+    workspace = {}
+    to_files(chat, workspace)
+
+    assert workspace["all_output.txt"] == chat
+
+    expected_files = {
+        "file1.py": 'print("Hello, World!")\n',
+        "file2.py": "def add(a, b):\n    return a + b\n",
+        "README.md": "\nThis is a sample program.\n\nfile1.py\n",
+    }
+
+    for file_name, file_content in expected_files.items():
+        assert workspace[file_name] == file_content
+
+
+def test_to_files_with_square_brackets():
+    chat = textwrap.dedent(
+        """
+    This is a sample program.
+
+    [file1.py]
+    ```python
+    print("Hello, World!")
+    ```
+
+    [file2.py]
+    ```python
+    def add(a, b):
+        return a + b
+    ```
+    """
+    )
+    workspace = {}
+    to_files(chat, workspace)
+
+    assert workspace["all_output.txt"] == chat
+
+    expected_files = {
+        "file1.py": 'print("Hello, World!")\n',
+        "file2.py": "def add(a, b):\n    return a + b\n",
+        "README.md": "\nThis is a sample program.\n\n[file1.py]\n",
+    }
+
+    for file_name, file_content in expected_files.items():
+        assert workspace[file_name] == file_content
+
+
+def test_files_with_brackets_in_name():
+    chat = textwrap.dedent(
+        """
+    This is a sample program.
+
+    [id].jsx
+    ```javascript
+    console.log("Hello, World!")
+    ```
+    """
+    )
+
+    workspace = {}
+    to_files(chat, workspace)
+
+    assert workspace["all_output.txt"] == chat
+
+    expected_files = {
+        "[id].jsx": 'console.log("Hello, World!")\n',
+        "README.md": "\nThis is a sample program.\n\n[id].jsx\n",
+    }
+
+    for file_name, file_content in expected_files.items():
+        assert workspace[file_name] == file_content
